title: Loss of Qualifying Coverage
summary: Job-based or other minimum essential coverage ended or will end, including many Medicaid/CHIP, Medicare Part A or MA, dependent, and discontinued-plan losses.
questions: Did you or anyone in your household lose health coverage, or expect to lose it soon?
What kind of coverage is ending, and what is the exact last day of coverage?
Why is it ending: a job or eligibility change, turning 26, loss of Medicaid or CHIP, loss of Medicare Part A or Medicare Advantage, or the plan ending?
Was the coverage voluntarily canceled, ended for nonpayment, or taken away because of fraud or missing information?
windowNote: Usually 60 days before or after the coverage loss; Medicaid or CHIP loss may allow 90 days after coverage ends.
priorCoverageNote: The coverage being lost must generally be qualifying coverage/MEC. Voluntary cancellation, nonpayment, fraud, or loss of non-MEC generally does not qualify.
cta: Likely SEP category: Loss of Qualifying Coverage, proceed to application

title: Change in Household Size
summary: Marriage, birth, adoption, foster placement, court-ordered dependent, or an Exchange-option loss of a dependent after divorce, legal separation, or death.
questions: Did anyone in your household get married, have or adopt a baby, place a child for foster care, or gain a dependent by court order?
What was the event date, and who joined or left the household?
If this was a marriage, did either spouse have qualifying health coverage for at least one day during the 60 days before the marriage?
If this involved divorce, legal separation, or death, did it also cause someone to lose coverage or dependent status?
windowNote: Generally 60 days after the household event; birth, adoption, foster placement, and court-order coverage may be retroactive to the event date.
priorCoverageNote: Marriage generally requires one spouse to have had qualifying coverage for at least 1 day in the prior 60 days, subject to CMS exceptions. The birth/adoption/foster/court-order pathways do not use that rule.
cta: Likely SEP category: Change in Household Size, proceed to application

title: Change in Primary Place of Living
summary: A qualifying move that gives the household access to new Marketplace plans, including certain school, seasonal-work, shelter, foreign-country, or territory moves.
questions: Did you permanently move to a new ZIP code or county, and what was the move date?
What were your old and new ZIP codes, and did the move give you access to different health plans?
Was this a move from another country or U.S. territory, for school or seasonal work, or to or from a shelter or transitional housing?
Did you have qualifying health coverage for at least one day during the 60 days before the move?
windowNote: Generally 60 days after the qualifying move. A vacation or move only for medical treatment does not qualify.
priorCoverageNote: Usually requires qualifying coverage for at least 1 day in the prior 60 days. Exceptions include certain moves from abroad or a U.S. territory, tribal/ANCSA status, or living where no Marketplace QHP was available.
cta: Likely SEP category: Change in Primary Place of Living, proceed to application

title: Change in Eligibility for Coverage/Financial Help
summary: A qualifying change involving Marketplace eligibility, APTC/CSR, lawful presence, release from incarceration, tribal status, AmeriCorps, or access to an ICHRA/QSEHRA.
questions: Are you currently enrolled through the Marketplace, and did your income or household information change your eligibility for premium help or cost-sharing reductions?
Did you recently become a U.S. citizen, national, or lawfully present, or were you released from incarceration?
Did you gain or maintain federally recognized tribal or ANCSA shareholder status, or start or end AmeriCorps service?
Did an employer newly offer you an ICHRA or QSEHRA, and what is its start date?
windowNote: Generally 60 days from the eligibility change; ICHRA/QSEHRA access may be reported within 60 days before or after its start.
priorCoverageNote: Requirements vary. Some income-change paths require current Marketplace enrollment; an Exchange-option income-decrease path may require other MEC for at least 1 day in the prior 60 days.
cta: Likely SEP category: Change in Eligibility for Coverage/Financial Help, proceed to application

title: Enrollment or Plan Error
summary: Marketplace or official assister error, technical delay, adverse plan-display error, or a material Marketplace plan contract violation.
questions: What plan or effective date did you expect, and what enrollment result did you actually receive?
Did the issue come from the Marketplace, an insurance company, agent, broker, Navigator, or another official enrollment helper?
Was there a technical delay or incorrect plan, benefit, service-area, cost-sharing, or premium information shown when you enrolled?
Do you have notices, screenshots, confirmation numbers, or other records showing the error or plan contract violation?
windowNote: This is not a simple automatic 60-day window; contact the Marketplace Call Center or CMS caseworker promptly so the error and available correction date can be determined.
priorCoverageNote: No blanket prior-coverage rule applies, but the Marketplace or CMS must confirm the qualifying Exchange error, material plan error, or contract violation.
cta: Likely SEP category: Enrollment or Plan Error, proceed to application

title: Other Qualifying Changes
summary: Exceptional circumstances, domestic abuse or abandonment, late Medicaid/CHIP denial, untimely notice, or the end of a COBRA subsidy or employer contribution.
questions: Did a disaster, serious medical condition, or another unexpected event keep you from enrolling on time?
Are you trying to enroll separately because of domestic abuse or spousal abandonment?
Were you denied Medicaid or CHIP after Open Enrollment or after another SEP window had already passed?
Did you receive late notice of a qualifying event, or did a COBRA subsidy or employer contribution completely end?
windowNote: Timing is event-specific rather than one automatic 60-day rule; document the event and contact the Marketplace promptly when Call Center or CMS review is required.
priorCoverageNote: Prior-coverage requirements vary by the specific event. The Marketplace application, eligibility notice, Call Center, or CMS caseworker makes the final determination.
cta: Likely SEP category: Other Qualifying Changes, proceed to application
